artboards.title: The whole Summary sheet, read as a dashboard
A+. Dashboard treatment of the header

annotations.text:
The Summary sheet as one dashboard, drawn from the McKellar-Sipes (MKL) example run: every number and every chart on it is a value the sheet already produces.
Six KPI tiles, bars inside the present-worth column, the locator map and the Google Earth export in one card, the seven charts on a two-column grid, and the unit-cost benchmark in the eighth cell.

Two things here are proposals, not what the workbook does today:
1. Chart 1's five categories use one light-to-dark ramp instead of the mixed greys, so the stack reads in order.
2. The eighth panel is new: it puts all four unit costs on one scale against published Tennessee runway work, so a quantity that is out by an order of magnitude shows up.
Everything else is already calculated.

Where the map should sit.
A keeps every row where it is; B reads louder but pushes the charts and the section block down about ten rows.
Both options carry the same new content: divisions on the map, and a line saying the unit costs are statewide while the Middle/West/East columns in Pay_Items sit empty.
Same placement, read as a dashboard. Six KPI tiles, bars inside the present-worth column, and a unit-cost benchmark. Nothing moves rows; every value already exists in a cell.
